title: Five Stages of Greek Religion (incl. Sallustius)
author: Gilbert Murray
description: Five Stages of Greek Religion by Gilbert Murray (1925, revised from his 1912 Four Stages), in the Project Gutenberg edition, which includes Murray's translation of the treatise On the Gods and the World by Sallustius. Murray, Regius Professor of Greek at Oxford, traces the development of Greek religion through five stages: the primitive 'Saturnia regna' of pre-Hellenic ritual; the Olympian conquest and the Homeric gods; the great age of philosophy and Plato and Aristotle; the 'failure of nerve' of the Hellenistic period, with its mystery cults, astrology and Gnosticism; and the last protest of paganism under the Emperor Julian. Sallustius's fourth-century catechism of Neoplatonic paganism explains the gods, myths, cosmos, fate and providence, sacrifice and the soul. It is a classic of the Cambridge Ritualist era and a concise primary source on late-antique pagan theology.
